name: nothing checks for cancellation before the handler starts
why: Both guards removed. A request cancelled while queued then reaches its handler, which waits for an abort that already fired and never answers. Either guard alone is enough, so the mutant has to remove both.

name: an older protocol version is accepted
why: Answering a version we do not speak looks like agreement and is not.

name: the required _meta fields are not required
why: Reading context from anywhere but the request is the connection state this version deleted.

name: a missing resource uses the retired code
why: -32002 was retired with 2025-11-25 and this version forbids emitting it.

name: progress is sent without a token
why: Progress the client never opted into invents a correlation it cannot use.

name: notifications outlive their request
why: A message after the response belongs to a request the client has finished with.

name: backpressure is never wired to the transport
why: The mechanism existed and was not connected, so every notification queued.

name: the concurrency limit is ignored
why: A limit nothing enforces is a number in a config file.

name: a settled request can still be aborted
why: A timer that fires after the response reopens a request that is over.

name: an empty input schema becomes null
replace: if (!schema) return null as unknown as JsonSchema;
why: inputSchema MUST be a JSON Schema object and MUST NOT be null.

name: the table sorts numbers as text
find: if (typeof a === "number" && typeof b === "number") return a - b;
why: 12 sorts after 143, which is the commonest table bug there is.

name: selection is not keyed to a stable row id
find:
const defaultId = (row: Row): string =>
  String(cell(row, "id") ?? JSON.stringify(row));
replace:
let counter = 0;
const defaultId = (_row: Row): string => String(counter++);
why: Selection is dropped whenever the row list is rebuilt, which filtering does.

name: a row cannot be selected from the keyboard
why: The table is operable by pointer only, which excludes anyone not using one.

name: aria-sort is not cleared from the other columns
find:
const sortState = computed(() =>
      sortKey() === column.key ? sortDirection() : "none");
why: Every column claims to be the sorted one, so a screen reader is told three contradictory things.

name: an effect tracks a branch it did not take
why: Dependencies accumulate instead of being re-collected, so unrelated changes cause renders. That is the rerun model with extra steps.

name: prefilling the form also submits it
why: The agent gets to press the button, and the human review the form represents becomes theatre.

name: a refused operation is swallowed
why: The button appears to work and does nothing, which is the commonest failure in the wild.

name: a metric colours its delta by sign alone
why: A rise in errors is shown as good, which is backwards half the time.

name: every toast is announced separately
replace: for (const m of messages) region.textContent = m;
why: A burst becomes twenty interruptions, which is unusable at any speed.

name: set() treats a function argument as an updater
why: A signal can no longer hold a function, so a computed returning a formatter silently calls it instead of storing it.

name: every tab sits in the tab order
why: Tab walks through every tab instead of moving past the list, which is the ARIA practice this claims to follow.

name: arrow keys do not move between tabs
find:
if (key === "ArrowRight") { event.preventDefault(); move(item.id, 1); }
        else if (key === "ArrowLeft") { event.preventDefault(); move(item.id, -1); }
why: The tab list is operable by pointer only.

name: hidden tab panels are built anyway
why: Six tabs fetch six times on open, which is the cost this laziness exists to avoid.

name: columns never collapse
why: A host handing out 300 pixels still gets side-by-side columns.

name: the contract stops carrying its output type
find: export type OutputOf<C> = C extends { output?: infer S } ? Infer<S> : unknown;
why: A view can read any field off any tool result again, which is the doubt the contract exists to remove.

name: the server is not checked against the contract
replace: export type Implementation<C extends Contracts, Ctx> = Record<string, (input: any, context: Ctx) => any>;
why: A server can return the wrong shape, or omit a declared tool, and nothing notices until a client calls it.

name: the typed client is optional-chained away
why: Every call needs `api.tool?.()`, which reintroduces exactly the doubt the contract removes.

name: proposing applies the change
replace:
pending.set(rationale === undefined ? { value } : { value, rationale });
      void options.onAccept(value);
why: The agent edits directly and the review the interface implies becomes decoration.

name: a high-risk approval needs no confirmation
why: Irreversible money movement is one click away, with nothing between the agent's request and the act.

name: an approval can be decided twice
why: A denied request can then be approved, which makes the record of what happened untrue.

name: cancelling a task rolls its progress back to zero
why: It says nothing happened, when three of five steps did and were not rolled back.

name: the stream announces every line
why: At five lines a second a screen reader reads everything aloud and the reader can do nothing else.

name: the stream speaks even when nothing arrived
why: A quiet log interrupts on a timer to say nothing happened.

name: a protocol refusal becomes a transport failure
find:
const status = "error" in response
      && response.error.code === CODE.invalidParams ? 400 : 200;
why: A version refusal is a well-formed answer carrying the list of versions the server does speak. Sent as a 400 it tells a proxy to retry what can never succeed, and hides that list behind a transport failure.

name: a malformed request is answered 200
find:
const status = "error" in response
      && response.error.code === CODE.invalidParams ? 400 : 200;
why: The one case the specification does put in the status line is a malformed request. Answering it 200 makes a request the server never understood indistinguishable from one it did.

name: a GET is answered like a POST
why: 2026-07-28 removed the GET endpoint along with sessions. A GET that falls through to the POST path answers a parse error instead of saying the method is not there.

name: a failed tool is handed to the view as a shape
why: The failure then arrives as an undefined `structuredContent`, which is the `?? []` the contract exists to delete. A tool that failed must raise, so the view cannot read a shape that was never returned.

name: arguments never reach the server
why: The typed call still type-checks and still resolves, and every filter, id and page argument a view sends is silently dropped on the way to the tool.

name: the sentence for the model never reaches the view
why: `content` and `structuredContent` are the two halves of one answer. A view that cannot see what the model was told cannot keep the two in agreement.

name: the dev host cannot refuse
why: A dev host that only ever succeeds teaches an application to assume it always will, and the first refusal then happens in front of a user. The switch is the reason this file exists.

name: the dev host logs only its own side of the conversation
why: What the view asked for disappears and only the answer is shown, so a call with the wrong arguments looks like a server that answered wrongly.

name: the host frame is given allow-same-origin
why: Every claim a view makes about the sandbox rests on the frame having an opaque origin. Weakening it changes nothing visible, which is exactly why the suite has to fail rather than the property quietly going away.

name: the action that needs a selection is offered without one
why: Restart is enabled with nothing selected, so activating it reads `table.selected()[0]`, finds nothing and returns having done nothing. A control that is offered has to do something.

name: the filter never narrows the rows
why: The filter draws, accepts typing and changes nothing. Filtering locally is the whole claim of the pane: the rows are already here, so narrowing them must not cost a tool call, and must actually narrow them.

name: every dialog answers to the same id
why: One dialog is fine and two are not: the second one's aria-labelledby resolves to the first one's heading, so it announces a title it is not showing. A view has as many dialogs as it has decisions to ask about.

name: two tab groups mint the same panel ids
why: Tab ids are the caller's and are local to their group, so two groups both holding a tab called `one` point at each other's panels.

name: the table filter has no name at all
why: Both names, because either alone is enough and removing one proves nothing. An unnamed search box is announced as `edit text` and the reader has to guess what typing there does.

name: a form label points at nothing
why: The label still draws, so it looks right and reads wrong: the control has no accessible name and clicking the label no longer focuses it.

name: the dismiss button loses its name
why: The glyph inside it is decoration, so the only way to dismiss a notification announces itself as an unnamed button.

name: the progress bar loses its name
why: Three tasks then expose three progress bars that say only a percentage, and nothing says which task each belongs to.

name: the high-risk confirmation loses its label
why: The field where a person types the title back to approve a high-risk action is the last thing that should be unlabelled.

name: a chart is a picture with no numbers behind it
why: The summary survives and the values do not, so a reader who cannot see the marks is told the shape of the answer instead of being given the answer.

name: arrow keys do not move through a chart
find:
if (key === "ArrowRight") { event.preventDefault(); move(1); }
        else if (key === "ArrowLeft") { event.preventDefault(); move(-1); }
why: The plot keeps its tab stop and stops being a route through the data, which is the difference between a result and a picture of one.

name: a chart speaks before anybody has moved
replace:
const row = current[index] ?? current[0];
    if (!row) return "";
why: The readout announces a point nobody is on the moment the chart mounts, and the cursor is drawn on it.

name: a chart is drawn once and never again
why: A panel whose tool answered again keeps drawing the previous answer. A dashboard refreshes one panel at a time, so this is the normal case rather than the edge one.

name: bars hang from the top of the frame
find:
y: Math.min(y, base),
        width: Math.max(1, each - 2),
        height: Math.max(1, Math.abs(base - y)),
replace:
y: top,
        width: Math.max(1, each - 2),
        height: Math.max(1, base - y),
why: Every bar starts at the top rather than on the axis, so a fall points the same way as a rise and the picture says the opposite of the number.

name: an area is never closed
why: The fill then runs to wherever the renderer decides to close the shape, which is not the axis.

name: a scatter chart plots by row order
why: The relationship the chart exists to show is replaced by the order the rows happened to arrive in.

name: a sparkline says nothing about its range
find:
const description = computed(() =>
    summaryOf(options.label, values(), format()));
why: A sparkline is too small to read a value off, so its name is the only place the numbers exist. Naming it after the field alone leaves nothing behind the picture.

name: a heatmap encodes value only as colour
why: Colour is not a channel every reader has, and lightness is not one anybody reads precisely. The cell keeps its shade and loses its number.

name: a chart takes the engine's locale
why: 1234567 renders as 1,234,567 in Chromium and 12,34,567 in WebKit on the same machine, so half the readers get a number they have to stop and parse.
